verdict.headline: Nvidia delivers the dual-bar beat; chip sector resets ahead of Warsh's keynote Friday
verdict.label: SPX -0.07% to 7,672; NVDA AH +5% to ~$220 on $96.2B revenue, 75% GM, $108B Q3 guide; PCE core 3.3% in-line; 10Y -10bps; AMD +4.91%; META $18B settlement
verdict.rationale_short: NVDA cleared both bars simultaneously — gross margin 75% (above 74.9%) and Q3 guide $108B (above $104.2B expected), ex-China. Core PCE at 3.3% preserved the rate backdrop: the 10Y fell 10bps to 4.64%, removing the multiple compression that preceded the print. The Q3 guide excluding China makes the $108B a floor, not a ceiling, if export policy eases; the China exclusion also caps the read-through if Huawei Ascend continues gaining share there. The session now shifts to Warsh's Friday keynote — a neutral-to-hold signal confirms the macro improvement; hawkish framing citing Canada tariff cost-push would push the 30Y back above 5.20% into a chip-sector post-NVDA window. If the 30Y crosses 5.25% before Friday close, this read no longer holds.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD at $479 has had nine consecutive sessions below the $484 structural ceiling. NVDA's dual-bar beat — GM 75% and Q3 guide $108B — removes the demand-skeptical scenario that was capping AMD's multiple alongside execution concerns. Raymond James raised the target to $641 on the $201B server-CPU forecast. Thursday is the first post-print session; the setup is the most favorable AMD has seen since early August.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive regular-session closes above $484 on above-average volume would confirm the ceiling has broken. Below $460 Thursday signals the market is treating NVDA's beat as isolated to the Blackwell stack, not a sector-wide read-through.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh hawkish keynote Friday pushing 30Y above 5.25% would add rate compression on top of the AMD multiple, capping any breakout regardless of NVDA's fundamental read.
trade_setups.horizon: Thursday through Friday close; Warsh keynote is the gating event.

trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y retreated from Tuesday's 5.23% to approximately 5.15% today after PCE core printed in-line. At 15bps below the 5.30% formal trigger, the yield has the most room it has had since early August. The Bessent long-dated buyback program ($4B+ per op) begins September 9; structural demand is coming. Warsh's Friday keynote is the next directional catalyst.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y holding below 5.20% through Friday would formally deactivate the rate-regime risk for the first time since mid-July. A sustained break above 5.25% into the Warsh keynote would re-trigger compression concerns heading into September FOMC.
trade_setups.invalidation: A hawkish Warsh keynote citing Canada tariff inflation and headline PCE at 3.7% is the direct path to 30Y back above 5.25%. If 30Y crosses 5.30%, the regime trigger reactivates in the same session as the post-NVDA chip reset.

trade_setups.thesis: BTC has had three consecutive sessions testing $80K — each with an intraday breach and a close below. The ceiling is structural. Two attempts preceded Wednesday's third; the debasement bid (DXY declining, Bessent Treasury buyback program) provides support from below. The ceiling and the floor are converging.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive regular-session closes above $80,000 would signal the ceiling breaking. Bessent's pending 'major financial institution' sanction, if targeting a Chinese bank Thursday, is the session's crypto-adjacent wildcard — a China-bank announcement historically produces a brief BTC spike followed by reversal. $76,661 (August 24 intraday low) is the support level that would signal the ceiling is reasserting as a range top.
trade_setups.invalidation: A hawkish Warsh driving yields sharply higher Friday, combined with no new crypto-specific catalyst, returns BTC to the lower end of the $76-78K range.
trade_setups.horizon: Thursday through Warsh Friday; then reassess at September 9 (buyback ops begin).

bear_case: The constructive scenario happened — but notice what it did not resolve. NVDA's Q3 guide of $108B explicitly excludes China data center revenue; if Huawei Ascend 910C continues gaining enterprise share in China, $108B becomes a ceiling rather than a floor. Gross margin at 75% is the second consecutive quarter of compression from the 78-80% peak range; if memory and wafer costs continue rising, higher revenue converts to margin compression rather than multiple expansion. CSCO (-4% AH on beat-and-raise) and AMAT (-3.9% AH on beat) demonstrated that AI infrastructure altitude does not guarantee multiple re-rate even on a clean print. NVDA's +5% AH on a bigger beat is more constructive but not unprecedented confirmation of sustained multiple expansion. If the 30Y crosses 5.25% following Warsh's Friday keynote, NVDA's expanded multiple faces rate compression from above and margin pressure from below simultaneously, and this read no longer holds.
